neighbours.label: a word piece that continues an unusual word right after a short first piece: the kanji after the honorific prefix お (お茶, お花), and inner consonant pieces of transliterated Slavic or Central Asian names (Pan|j|shir, L|j|ub|lj|ana)
fire: 週末は友達とお茶を飲みながら話しました。
父は夕食のときはお酒を少しだけ飲みます。
母の誕生日にはいつもお花を買って帰ります。
暑い日は冷たいお水をこまめに飲んでください。
The convoy drove north through the Panjshir valley at dawn.
Last spring the conference was held in Ljubljana for the first time.
The ferry from Sweden arrives in the port of Szczecin every morning.
Many historians have studied the advice that Brzezinski gave the president.
quiet: 週末は友達とコーヒーを飲みながら話しました。
父は夕食のときはビールを少しだけ飲みます。
母の誕生日にはいつもケーキを買って帰ります。
暑い日は冷たいジュースをこまめに飲んでください。
The convoy drove north through the Rhine valley at dawn.
Last spring the conference was held in Vienna for the first time.
The ferry from Sweden arrives in the port of Hamburg every morning.
Many historians have studied the advice that Kissinger gave the president.

predictions: fire 0.5-0.85 on the kanji after お and on 'j'/'cz'/'ze' pieces inside transliterated names; the same nouns without お around 0.25, and common English names below 0.05
short: piece after お / inside foreign names
notes: Card: '手' x7 (お手伝い), '天' (お天気), '仕' (お仕事), 'd' in Pajdusakova, 'j' in Panjwai, 'ith' in Pithana, ' 이름'. Probe: お手伝い 0.752, お天気 0.824, お仕事 0.816; without お 0.251 and 0.277; Pajdusakova 0.859, Panjwai 0.686; 'Mrkos and Smith' 0.025. The shared pattern is a continuation piece after an odd prefix; the near misses keep the noun or the frame and drop the split. Without-お near misses are a known risk near 0.25.
